A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Model-Informed Flow research. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and matchable despite the shortened title and section reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original variational-inference results, component ablations, and network-capacity experiments in Tables 1–3 and Figures 1–2.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds training-time measurements in Appendix D.3, Tables 6–7.

M1.justification: The MIF transformation, prior inputs, translation network, topological ordering, objective, and Algorithms 1–2 are unchanged. The timing experiments evaluate existing architectural variants.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same nine benchmarks. The added timing study uses six existing hierarchical benchmarks; the new Poisson/Binomial example in Section 2.2 is explanatory, not an evaluated task.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 1–3 is unchanged. The new timing comparisons reuse the existing noise-conditioned and no-translation MIF variants, labeled 'MIF with ε' and '2 networks (no t)'.

E3.justification: Appendix D.3 adds wall-clock training time as an evaluation measure, comparing variants at 0, 64, 256, 512, and 1024 hidden units. The original ELBO experiments retain their training budgets, sample counts, optimizer, and learning-rate search.

E4.justification: Tables 6–7 supplement the existing accuracy ablations with computational-cost analyses of latent versus noise conditioning and three versus two conditioning networks. The original component ablations and expressiveness analysis remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added timing tables likewise provide point values without uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and Figures 1–2 retain their results. Tables 6–7 add runtime results: for MovieLens with 1024 hidden units, default MIF takes 15,873.45 seconds, the noise-conditioned variant 6,749.33, and the no-translation variant 14,687.99. These are new efficiency measurements, not ELBO improvements.

T1.justification: The core flow definitions, Theorem 4, Corollary 6, Lemma 7, and Appendix C proofs are unchanged. The added hierarchical-model example and expanded nonlinearity explanation illustrate the existing mathematics without revising its formal results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same central claims: representing full-rank VIP through an augmented autoregressive flow and obtaining competitive posterior approximations. The shortened title does not change the scientific contribution.

C2.justification: The interpretations of prior information, conditioning, and network capacity remain unchanged, as does the limitation concerning sequential sampling and parallel efficiency. Appendix D.3 reports timing trends without introducing a different mechanism explanation or applicability boundary.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit implementation-repository link in Section 5.1 and documents training times and benchmark latent dimensions in Tables 6–7. Hardware specifications and the conditioning-network implementation were already documented in v1.

R1.justification: The same 43 references are retained, along with the positioning relative to VIP, ASVI, Cascading Flows, and Embedded-Model Flows. The rewritten and relocated related-work section does not substantively change this positioning.

P1.justification: v2 shortens the title, expands Section 2.2 with parent-set clarification and a worked example, and lightly rewrites related work into a separate section preceding experiments. It also adds acknowledgements and Appendix D.3; most existing prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds two grouped runtime tables and relocates Table 3 to a separate page. Existing figures and table designs remain substantially unchanged, with surrounding text reflowing around the additions.

improvement.justification: The new timing analyses quantify a computational limitation that v1 discussed only qualitatively. Together with explicit code-access information and the explanatory model example, they improve practical assessment and clarity. The main scientific evidence remains unchanged, and timing uncertainty is still unreported, so the overall gain is limited.
